original_question: Let T be a positive subtree of 2^{<ω}, meaning that [T] has measure greater than 0. Let P denote the statement that every positive tree has a perfect subtree, and let P^- denote the statement that every positive tree has infinitely many pairwise distinct paths X_n in [T]. Over RCA_0, does P^- imply P?
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Wei Wang), Problem 10: after defining the principles P^+, P, and P^- for positive binary trees, the paper asks whether RCA_0 proves P^- -> P.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact open problem in the paper: it uses the correct ambient tree space 2^{<ω}, the correct positivity condition that [T] has positive measure, the correct two principles P and P^-, and the correct reverse-mathematical question over RCA_0 asking whether P^- implies P.
missing_details: The paper takes trees to be binary trees T ⊆ 2^{<ω}, with [T] denoting the set of infinite paths through T in 2^ω; this should be stated explicitly.
The measure on [T] should be identified as the usual product (fair-coin/Lebesgue) measure on Cantor space 2^ω.
The principle P should explicitly say that there exists a subtree S ⊆ T that is perfect; otherwise the subtree relation is only implicit.
For stand-alone clarity, 'perfect subtree' should be defined, e.g. every node of S has two incompatible extensions in S (equivalently, [S] is a perfect subset of 2^ω).

The principle P^- is more precise if written as: for every positive tree T there exists a sequence (X_n)_{n∈ω} of pairwise distinct members of [T]; 'infinitely many paths' is correct but slightly less formal.
To match the paper's reverse-mathematical phrasing exactly, the question should be stated as 'Does RCA_0 prove P^- -> P?' rather than only informally asking whether P^- implies P.
It helps to note, in line with the paper's surrounding definitions, that P does not require the perfect subtree itself to remain positive; that stronger variant is the separate principle P^+.
refined_question: Over the base system RCA_0, let T ⊆ 2^{<ω} be a binary tree, let [T] ⊆ 2^ω denote its set of infinite paths, and call T positive if μ([T]) > 0 for the usual product measure μ on 2^ω. Define P to be the statement that every positive tree T has a perfect subtree S ⊆ T, where 'perfect' means that every node of S has two incompatible extensions in S. Define P^- to be the statement that every positive tree T has a sequence (X_n)_{n∈ω} of pairwise distinct paths in [T]. Does RCA_0 prove P^- -> P?
justification: This is the exact problem asked in the paper. In Section 5, Wei Wang first defines positive trees and the three principles P^+, P, and P^-, then immediately asks in Problem 10 whether RCA_0 proves P^- -> P. So your draft is already aimed at the right target. The only sharpening needed is to make explicit the standard Cantor-space conventions hidden in the paper's notation: [T] as the path set, μ as the usual product measure, S ⊆ T as the sought subtree, the meaning of 'perfect', and the sequence quantifier in P^-. I have not broadened the question to the stronger P^+ principle or to the dimension analogue, because those are treated separately in the same section, with the dimension version posed as Problem 11 rather than folded into Problem 10.
